articles.title: Welding AI Maker Path Robotics Raises $300M Series E With NAVER Ventures
articles.snippet: Welding AI Maker Path Robotics Raises $300M Series E With NAVER Ventures Wowtale
articles.text:
Skilled welders are hard to find, and shipyards and heavy-equipment plants are sitting on full order books. Traditional industrial robots do not help much here. They follow pre-programmed paths, which makes them a poor fit for welds that differ slightly from one part to the next. Path Robotics , a Columbus, Ohio-based startup, is betting that a robot that can see and decide for itself can fill that gap. On Nov. 10, the company announced a $300 million Series E at a $2.45 billion post-money valuation.
Georgian , an AI-focused growth equity firm, led the round. NAVER Ventures and D. E. Shaw Ventures joined as new investors, and existing backers Addition, Drive Capital, IronArc Ventures, Tiger Global, and Yamaha Motor Ventures also took part. Georgian partner Emily Walsh will join Path’s board.
Giving the robot eyes and judgment
A conventional welding robot has to be taught its path step by step, and a part that sits slightly out of place can ruin the weld. Path’s physical AI welding model, Obsidian, takes that teaching out of the loop. The robot finds the weld joint on its own, plans the sequence and path, welds, and adjusts when conditions change mid-job. The model learns from real-world welding data. For a factory, that means variable welds without reprogramming the robot each time.
The company recently added Rove, a mobile welding system that puts Obsidian on a quadruped robot. Instead of bringing the part to a welding cell, the robot walks to the part. Path says it shows the same model can run on different robot bodies.
ARR up 17x in 18 months, led by shipbuilding and defense
Path says its annual recurring revenue grew 17-fold over the past 18 months, though it did not disclose a dollar figure. The growth has come from shipbuilding and defense, heavy equipment, and energy infrastructure. Customers include HII, the largest U.S. shipbuilder, Lockheed Martin, and the maritime defense company Saronic , along with mid-sized manufacturers such as EK Machine, Millerbernd Manufacturing, TransAmerican Power Products, and TYCROP. Earlier this year, Path announced a $600 million performance-based production agreement with HII to deploy physical AI across U.S. Navy shipbuilding programs. Headcount has grown 97% over the past year, and the company plans to reach 400 employees by year-end.
CEO and co-founder Andy Lonsberry said Path started with welding because it is one of the hardest jobs on the factory floor to automate. “Our goal isn’t to automate one step, but to automate the entire factory,” he said. Founded in 2018, Path has now raised more than $610 million. The new money will go toward scaling the welding business, expanding to tasks before and after welding and to new robot form factors, and training AI models.
Georgian pointed to Path’s proprietary models and its growing base of production data, which it said improves the system with every deployment. Lockheed Martin Ventures called the investment an important milestone for strengthening the U.S. defense industrial base.
Competition: welding specialists and general-purpose robot AI
A handful of newer companies are going after the same problem. Korea’s RB-Ware makes a no-code welding robot and has installed more than 250 units in 16 countries, and NeoArcRobotics is building cutting and welding robots for Korean shipyards. Crypto financing announcements have totaled approximately $408.55 million across nine disclosed transactions during Nov. 7–13, 2026, led by a reported $270 million commitment to the bank-backed stablecoin venture Project Faro.
Summary
Nine disclosed financings totaled $408.55 million, including bank commitments and two public token sales.
Project Faro drew approximately $270 million in reported commitments for five years of operations.
Index Industries raised $50 million in seed funding led by Lightspeed Venture Partners.
Alta secured a $47.5 million Series A, bringing its cumulative funding to $80 million.
Project Faro, Index and Alta accounted for nearly 90% of the disclosed weekly total.
The tally includes corporate funding commitments and public token sales alongside venture rounds. Four further announcements covered cumulative or undisclosed funding.
DefiLlama’s funding database provided the weekly inventory, with company announcements, investor disclosures and reporting used to check transaction details.
Project Faro leads crypto financing with $270 million commitment
Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Santander and Deutsche Bank were among institutions committing around $270 million to a stablecoin venture , as crypto.news reported, citing Bloomberg’s Nov. 10 report.
Known as Project Faro, the proposed business would use the capital to cover five years of operating costs. The figure represents committed corporate financing, with no announcement that the full amount has been paid.
The 21-member consortium expects to establish its issuer in the United States. Its stated launch window is the first half of 2027, beginning with a dollar stablecoin intended for payments and digital asset settlement. A euro token is planned later.

Index Industries emerged from stealth on Nov. 10 with a $50 million seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Polychain Capital, Galaxy Ventures and Wintermute Ventures participated.
Founded by former Polychain president Josh Rosenthal and Longmark CEO Brian Hardecker, the company is developing a daily U.S. home-price index and tokenization infrastructure for housing-linked investment products.
Its first planned application is USHP, issued separately by British Virgin Islands-based USHP Limited. The issuer plans an Ethereum release in 2026 and a Solana expansion in 2027.
The announcement states that the referenced securities are unregistered in the United States and cannot be offered to U.S. persons without registration or an applicable exemption.

Alta announced a $47.5 million Series A led by Index Ventures on Nov. 10, with GV, Blackbird Ventures, Square Peg and Capital49 participating.

Sanofi-backed Windward Bio raises $225 million in its Nasdaq IPO as Rezera postpones its listing
Nov 13, 2026
·

By MLQ.ai Newsroom · Edited by Peter Foy
·
2 min read
Key points
Windward sold 10,294,117 shares at $17 and Sanofi bought $50 million of shares and pre-funded warrants at the same price, for $225 million in expected gross proceeds [1] .
Its lead drug, WIN378, a TSLP antibody licensed from China's Kelun Biotech, is in a Phase 2/3 asthma trial with results expected next year [2] .
Rezera postponed its $200 million IPO of 16.7 million shares at $11 to $13 [3] [4] .
Windward Bio Group priced its initial public offering of 10,294,117 shares at $17 each on Nov. 12, the midpoint of its $16 to $18 range, and sold an additional $50 million of shares and pre-funded warrants to Sanofi in a concurrent private placement at the same price [1] [5] . Gross proceeds are expected to total $225 million before fees and before the underwriters' option on 1,544,117 more shares [1] . The stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Friday under the symbol WWB, and the deal is set to close on Nov. 16 [1] .
Boston-based Rezera postponed a planned $200 million IPO on the evening of Nov. 11, citing market conditions, according to IPOScoop [4] . Jefferies and TD Cowen were bookrunners on both deals, alongside Piper Sandler and UBS for Windward and Cantor Fitzgerald for Rezera [1] [3] .
Two drugs licensed from China
Windward, formed two years ago, raised $365 million of venture funding before the IPO [2] . Its lead drug, WIN378, is an ultra-long-acting injectable that blocks TSLP, the same inflammatory protein targeted by AstraZeneca and Amgen's Tezspire, and could be dosed as rarely as twice a year against Tezspire's monthly schedule [2] . Windward licensed it from Kelun Biotech, which co-developed it with Harbour BioMed [2] . The Phase 3 part of an asthma trial began in September with results expected next year, and a mid-stage COPD study started in June with data due in 2027 [2] . A second drug, WIN027, licensed from Qyuns Therapeutics, targets both TSLP and IL-13 [2] . Windward paid $70 million upfront in cash and equity for the two programs and owes up to $1.6 billion more in milestone payments [2] .
Windward is the biotech sector's 30th IPO this year, according to BioPharma Dive, which counts 2026 as the busiest year for drugmaker listings since 2021, with more than $8 billion raised [2] .
Rezera steps back
Rezera, formerly NodThera, develops oral NLRP3 inhibitors for inflammatory diseases and describes itself as Phase 3-ready [3] [4] . It had planned to sell 16.7 million shares at $11 to $13 on the Nasdaq under the symbol RZRA, and GSK had indicated interest in buying up to $25 million of the offering, about 13% of the deal [3] . Its last amended registration statement was filed with the SEC on Nov. 9 [6] . The company has not said when it might return. The postponement came in the same week that Anthropic's bankers weighed pricing its IPO above its marketed range.

articles.title: Midwest startups raise $213.5 million in a week. Where is the money going?
articles.snippet: Midwest startups raise $213.5 million in a week. Where is the money going? Techli
articles.text:
Four of six deals are reported in Chicago, and the region is experiencing the latest funding activity in the form of investments in AI infrastructure and financial services.
According to StartMidwest’s funding roundup , $213.5 million was raised in six deals by Midwest startups and financial technology companies during the week ending Nov. 6, with two $100 million rounds accounting for almost all the capital.
Ocient, an AI infrastructure firm in Chicago, and Erebor Bank, which is based in Columbus, Ohio, were the leaders of the activity. The remaining included health care technology, artificial intelligence and fintech firms, reflecting the diversity of sectors that are being invested in all over the region.
The headline figure, however, requires some qualification: Erebor Bank’s $100 million investment from Japan’s SBI Holdings was announced as a planned commitment, not a completed financing round. The difference is important in evaluating the amount of capital that actually has flowed to companies in the Midwest.
The biggest round up to date was Ocient’s $100 million Series C , which was announced on November 5. The investment, led by BOKA Capital and OCA Ventures, totals $260 million for the Chicago firm. Other investors who were on board included existing investors Greycroft, In-Q-Tel, Blue Bear Capital, Buoyant Ventures, PSP Growth, Pritzker Group Venture Capital and Eron Wolf. Dallas Venture Capital joined as a new investor.
Ocient is a company that creates data analytics and AI solutions for enterprises dealing with vast amounts of data. The new investment will allow it to continue developing its OcientAIQ solutions that enable enterprises to deploy AI agents and analytics in petabyte-scale data environments.
Reliable, governed data is becoming a key infrastructure need as businesses delve into agentic AI systems that can analyze information and execute tasks. Ocient claims its solution can be used for data governance along with high-performance data analytics, enabling AI agents and analysts to ask questions about the data in a customer’s environment.
The company anticipates that its revenue will more than triple in 2026 due to the demand of customers with growing and high-volume data sets. This projection is not a financial result but an estimate by Ocient.
The second $100 million was from a digital bank called Erebor Bank, based in Columbus, Ohio, which offers services to companies in fields such as artificial intelligence, robotics and advanced manufacturing, defense, and energy. The timing of the completion of the investment was not mentioned in the funding roundup, but SBI Holdings revealed its plan to invest $100 million .
Four of the six transactions were in Chicago. In addition to Ocient, medical technology firm Focused Medical Technologies, a treatment developer for pulmonary embolism, secured $6 million in investment, including two medical technology strategic investors and UCM Ventures. The University of Chicago startup is targeting the funds for product development, manufacturing and setting up for a pivotal study in the United States.
Consumer insights firm QualSights raised $5 million in funding, led by Duo Partners. The company employs smart sensors and a consumer application and AI analytics to provide a better understanding of how humans use physical products. The funding came with the appointment of Prasanna Pitale as Chief Executive.

Patrick raised its dividend while merger covenants block use of the renewed buyback capacity.
The repurchase authorization sits idle because the pending LCI merger restricts Patrick from buying its own stock.
Patrick balances shareholder returns against funding organic growth and acquisitions from its cash generation.
Patrick Industries ( PATK ) announced on November 13, 2026 that its board had increased the quarterly common-stock dividend to $0.52 per share from $0.47 and replenished its share-repurchase authorization to $200 million. The announcement pairs a higher cash payout with additional repurchase capacity that cannot currently be used because of covenants in Patrick’s pending all-stock merger with LCI Industries ( LCII ) .
The board approved the dividend increase on November 11, 2026. The new rate is approximately 10.6% above the previous rate, calculated from the announced per-share amounts. The dividend is payable on December 7, 2026, to shareholders of record at the close of business on November 23, 2026.
Repurchase Capacity Remains Restricted
The authorization covers repurchases over the next 24 months and includes $61.9 million that remained under the previous authorization. The board therefore added $138.1 million of capacity, calculated as the difference between the new total and the remaining amount.
The repurchase program cannot presently be used. Patrick entered into the LCI merger agreement on June 30, 2026, and its operating covenants restrict repurchases of Patrick common stock. The company expects those restrictions to remain in place while the agreement is in effect.
The restrictions were already visible in Patrick’s third-quarter report , which said the company made no share repurchases during the quarter because of the merger agreement. The SEC declared the merger registration statement effective on October 19, 2026, and Patrick has scheduled a special shareholder meeting for November 18, 2026.
Cash Flow and Capital Allocation
Chief Executive Officer Andy Nemeth said the decisions were grounded in Patrick’s capital allocation, cash generation and balance sheet. “Since initiating our quarterly dividend in 2019, we have raised it each year and have been active with share repurchases, deploying $106.1 million in the first nine months of 2026,” he said.
Returning capital is only one use of that cash. Nemeth said cash generation through the cycle also enables investment in organic initiatives and strategic mergers and acquisitions, which Patrick expects to remain a priority.
The latest results provide context for those competing demands. Third-quarter net sales were $975 million, compared with $976 million a year earlier, while operating income declined to $50 million from $66 million. For the first nine months of 2026, operating cash flow was $147 million, down from $199 million in the prior-year period. Patrick attributed the change to working-capital deployment supporting its composite-products growth strategy and inventory management for customers.

Asset Based Lending Announces Fourth Securitization of $200 Million, Marking Largest Transaction to Date
News provided by
Asset Based Lending, LLC
Nov 12, 2026, 13:33 ET
Share this article
Share this article
JERSEY CITY, N.J. , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Asset Based Lending (ABL) , a national private lender and a driving force behind the next generation of real estate investment, has successfully closed its fourth unrated securitization, totaling $200 million. The transaction, ABL 2026 RTL-1, which priced on October 15 and closed on October 26, marks ABL's largest to date, bringing its cumulative securitization volume to $723 million.
The transaction is backed by a diversified pool of business-purpose residential real estate loans, with an industry-leading concentration of ground-up infill construction loans. This reflects ABL's 16 years of experience in ground-up construction lending and its proven ability to manage the complexities and risks of residential development.
"We are proud to lead the industry in financing ground-up construction, and to do it at a cost that keeps our pricing competitive for the builders we serve," said Kevin Rodman, CEO of ABL. "This transaction underscores the strength of the platform our team has built and the confidence investors have in our credit. Every one of these loans puts new housing on the ground."
The transaction also demonstrates ABL's ability to navigate challenging market conditions. Despite heightened volatility and increased investor selectivity across the securitization market, ABL secured competitive financing terms. The deal reached the market in approximately three weeks, making it one of the company's fastest securitization executions.
Performance Trust Capital Partners, LLC served as structuring agent, with Nomura Securities International, Inc. ("Nomura") and Mizuho Securities USA LLC serving as joint bookrunners.
"Successfully executing this transaction amid market volatility reinforces the effectiveness of our capital markets strategy and the quality of our platform," said Daniel Gotay, Head of Capital Markets at ABL. "We have built durable relationships with institutional investors and established a track record they can underwrite, giving us consistent access to capital. For our borrowers, that is what matters most: they can count on ABL to fund their projects from start to finish."
The securitization also reflects ABL's expanding national footprint, with collateral spanning the Northeast, Sun Belt, Rust Belt and South. This geographic diversification supports the company's strategy to continue growing beyond its established Northeast presence and finance residential development in markets across the country.
To learn more about ABL, please visit www.ablfunding.com .
About Asset Based Lending
Asset Based Lending was established in 2010, providing fast bridge financing to real estate investors for the purchase, renovation, new construction, and long-term refinance of single-family, multi-family, and mixed-use properties. A trusted lender to thousands of investors, Asset Based Lending has closed over $4.4 billion in loans since its founding. Learn more at https://www.ablfunding.com/ . Follow the company on LinkedIn .

African startups raised a total of $183 million in October 2026 through 34 funding deals worth at least $100,000 each, according to the monthly report published on November 5 by investment tracking platform Africa: The Big Deal.
The amount represents a 24% decline compared with September and stands 29% below the average monthly funding of $259 million recorded over the past 12 months.
The slowdown was even more pronounced year-on-year. Funding fell by 58% from the $435 million raised by African startups in October 2025. The number of announced transactions also declined, with 34 deals recorded in October, against a monthly average of 43 over the past year.
Equity financing accounts for 60% of October funding
Equity investments dominated fundraising activity, accounting for $110 million, or 60% of the total raised during the month.
Debt financing amounted to $71 million, representing 39% of total funding, while grants accounted for approximately $2 million.
The two largest transactions each reached $40 million and were concluded outside Africa’s four leading startup funding markets: Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa.
In Morocco, health tech company ABA Life secured a $40 million investment agreement with pan-African investment fund Admaius Capital Partners.
Founded in 2021, the company develops solutions combining artificial intelligence, medical technologies, telemedicine and connected healthcare infrastructure. The funding will support its artificial intelligence programme for healthcare systems and facilitate its international expansion.
In Tanzania, agritech platform East Africa Foods raised nearly $40 million to expand its processing, storage and logistics capabilities, as well as its digital tools.
The company works with more than 28,000 small-scale farmers and supplies over 10,000 urban retailers. It plans to use the financing to expand into additional East African markets.
Nigeria leads African startup funding
Nigeria topped the continental ranking in October, with nine startups raising a combined $42 million, primarily through debt financing in the energy and mobility sectors.
Morocco and Tanzania followed with $40 million each, largely driven by the two major transactions involving ABA Life and East Africa Foods.
Egypt ranked fourth with $19 million, followed by Senegal with $13 million.
A notable shift in funding distribution was also recorded. Startups based in Africa’s four largest funding markets attracted just 46% of total capital raised in October, their lowest monthly share since November 2022.
